title: Indexing the adjacency word
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A$ be a Boolean-valued function on pairs of indices in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Form a list by concatenating, for each first index in increasing order, the values of $A$ at that index and all second indices in increasing order. The entry at zero-based position $un+v$, taking the default value to be false if the position is out of range, is $A(u,v)$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean-valued function on pairs of indices below $n$
